newsitem.title: USA: Citgo had fire Fri in Louisiana refinery-regulator.
newsitem.headline: Citgo had fire Fri in Louisiana refinery-regulator.

text.p: Citgo Petroleum Corp, the wholly-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA unit, had a fire Friday evening in the "number two" coker unit at its Lake Charles, Louisiana refinery, according a state regulators there.
A Citgo spokesman confirmed that the fire occurred, saying the unit would be down for an unspecified amount of time, and that two people at the plant suffered minor injuries.

"The fire was put out within 30 minutes by the internal fire fighting force," said Gerald Quarles, an official with the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality's Office of Air Quality and Radiation Protection.
The capacity of the affected coking unit could not be immediately confirmed.
The Lake Charles refinery has total crude distillation capacity of 305,000 barrels per day (bpd), and about 130,000 bpd of fluid catalytic cracking capacity.
According to industry sources, the company conducted maintenance on certain units at the refinery, including a hydrocracker and some reformers during the first few weeks of the year.
